step1_analysis.description: This passive LC network represents the common-mode filtering path connected to the center tap of a differential transformer's primary winding. It is designed to create a transmission zero (low impedance) at the 2nd harmonic to suppress common-mode harmonics in a C-band power amplifier.

paper_reference.title: A Bandpass Power Amplifier Applying Transformer-Based Filtering Combiner in 0.5-µm GaAs pHEMT

Z_cm_fundamental.description: Common-mode impedance at the fundamental frequency (6 GHz)

sky130_expected.reasoning: Should be relatively high to avoid loading the fundamental signal.

Z_cm_harmonic.description: Common-mode impedance at the 2nd harmonic frequency (12 GHz)

sky130_expected.reasoning: Should be low to act as a trap/short for the 2nd harmonic.

output_power.description: Saturated output power of the PA

sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 1.8V devices would yield lower output power than GaAs pHEMT.
Typical PAE for CMOS PAs at C-band.
CMOS typically has lower gain per stage than GaAs.

harmonic_suppression.description: Suppression of harmonics relative to fundamental (Spurious)

sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on the depth of the transmission zero created by this filter.

center_tap_inductance.description: Inductance connecting to the center of the primary winding

sky130_expected.reasoning: Directly from paper, used for harmonic trap.
Not a standard metric for RF PAs; likely a parsing error in the source metadata.

step3_testbench.description: Measures the common-mode impedance of the harmonic suppression filter at the fundamental (6 GHz) and 2nd harmonic (12 GHz).
step3_testbench.spice:
* Harmonic Suppression Filter Testbench

.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* DUT (Passive components with estimated values for 6GHz resonance, L4 from paper)
L1 n0 GND 1n
L2 n1 label_net_0 1n
L3 n0 n3 1n
L4 n1 n2 0.225n
L5 n1 label_net_1 1n
C1 n3 GND 1p
C2 n2 n3 1p

* Common-mode excitation (representing even-mode harmonics from PA drains)
V1 label_net_0 GND DC 0.9 AC 1
V2 label_net_1 GND DC 0.9 AC 1

.control
ac dec 100 1G 20G

* Calculate common-mode impedance
* Total common-mode current is the sum of currents from V1 and V2
let I_cm = mag(i(V1) + i(V2))
let Z_cm = 1 / I_cm

* Measure impedance at fundamental (6 GHz) and 2nd harmonic (12 GHz)
meas ac Z_cm_6G find Z_cm at=6G
meas ac Z_cm_12G find Z_cm at=12G

print Z_cm_6G Z_cm_12G
quit
.endc
.end
